parts.label: Map
parts.title: Follow personal data through the AI service
parts.body:
A useful data map starts before the prompt. Record collection, transcription, preprocessing, retrieval index, model request, provider logs, outputs, analytics, human review, deletion, and backup. Name the entity controlling each step, the purpose, data categories, access roles, storage and processing locations, retention, and subcontractors. A model's 'no training' setting answers one question; it says little about transient processing, abuse monitoring, logs, or backup retention.

Classify information by actual sensitivity and obligations. A customer call can contain identifiers, health details, payment data, and employee remarks even when the project is described as simple summarization. Minimize fields and test with synthetic or suitably de-identified records until the legitimate production use is established. Set separate boundaries for public, internal, confidential, and regulated material; classification names alone do not authorize transfer to a supplier.

For a Vancouver and Berlin rollout, map the Canadian entity and applicable federal or provincial law, and the EU controller and processor roles under GDPR. Legal and privacy specialists should identify lawful grounds and contractual terms. Residence in a chosen region is a useful design fact, but data access, onward transfer, purpose, retention, and rights still need analysis.

example.title: The hidden retention path
example.body: A vendor promises EU storage for customer-call transcripts, yet application telemetry includes snippets available to support staff elsewhere. The data map exposes the second path. The team restricts telemetry, revises processor terms, and verifies deletion before using live recordings.

exercise.title: Draw a data flow
exercise.body: Map a call summarizer from recording to deletion. For each hop, name controller or supplier, data class, purpose, access, location, retention, and evidence. Circle the hops whose contractual or technical facts are unknown and block a live-data pilot.

sources: Office of the Privacy Commissioner: Canadian privacy laws

parts.label: Assess
parts.title: Ask whether the use is justified and proportionate
parts.body:
Privacy review begins with a specified purpose and a lawful basis or authority where applicable. Ask whether the source data was collected for this use, whether people were informed as required, whether the same benefit can be achieved with less data, and how individuals can exercise relevant rights. EU GDPR analysis includes lawful basis, minimization, transparency, processor terms, rights, security, and international transfers where applicable. A data protection impact assessment may be required for processing likely to result in high risk. Counsel should determine this for the actual processing.

Canadian private-sector coverage varies. PIPEDA governs many commercial activities, while substantially similar provincial laws apply in some contexts in Alberta, British Columbia, and Québec; other sector and public-sector rules may also apply. Federal PIPEDA cannot be presumed to govern every employee record or provincial public service. Have Canadian privacy counsel identify the organization, activity, province, and cross-border flow. The federal public-sector automated-decision directive has a separate scope.

A defensible decision names the business purpose, candidate alternatives, expected benefit, residual privacy risk, and control owner. If a service wants to train on support calls, treat that as a distinct purpose from producing a customer's summary, with a separate approval and notice or other lawful basis as required.

example.title: Reduce collection
example.body: A sales manager wants full call recordings in a shared AI workspace to extract three action items. The team tests a restricted transcript path, excludes payment details, limits access to the account team, and sets a deletion schedule. Privacy counsel reviews the actual notices, lawful ground, and vendor terms before production.

exercise.title: Compare two designs
exercise.body: Write a purpose statement and compare full-recording upload with a minimized transcript workflow. For each, list benefit, sensitive data, retention, people affected, and missing legal facts. Recommend a pilot boundary and the owner who can approve it.

sources: Office of the Privacy Commissioner: PIPEDA in brief
Office of the Privacy Commissioner: summary of Canadian privacy laws

parts.label: Control
parts.title: Make a supplier's promises testable
parts.body:
Procurement should seek a data-processing description that matches the architecture: permitted purpose, processor and subprocessor roles, training use, security measures, region, access by support staff, retention and deletion, incident notice, audit evidence, and what happens at exit. Validate critical claims in product settings and test accounts. A contract clause is useful evidence of an obligation; it cannot stop an application from sending the wrong data through a broad connector.

Limit access by identity and task. Separate development, evaluation, and production data. Redact or tokenize fields where the task allows, encrypt transit and storage, restrict logs, and set deletion checks. Test retrieval boundaries across tenants and user roles; a model that answers from another customer's documents has already crossed a privacy boundary even if it never sends data to an outside domain.

Ask the supplier how model or service changes affect the data flow and who receives notice. Record subprocessors and transfer mechanisms for EU personal data where relevant. Canadian cross-border processing also needs an applicable-law and accountability review. Use privacy counsel for legal conclusions and security for technical verification; the business owner remains accountable for the use.

example.title: A procurement acceptance test
example.body: Before connecting Berlin calls, the team requests the vendor's subprocessor list and deletion terms, disables training use in the contracted service, tests that a Berlin agent cannot retrieve Vancouver transcripts, and verifies which logs persist after a deletion request.

exercise.title: Write eight supplier questions
exercise.body: Cover processing purpose, training, access, logs, deletion, subprocessors, transfers, incident notice, and exit. For each answer, name a contract term, product setting, or test that would verify it. Mark any unknown that prevents live data use.

sources: European Data Protection Board: AI models and GDPR opinion
Canadian privacy regulators: generative AI principles

parts.label: Decide
parts.title: Approve a bounded data use and watch for drift
parts.body:
The release decision should specify approved source systems, data classes, purposes, users, supplier configuration, regions, retention, and onward uses. A new connector, customer population, analytics feature, or model-training option is a material change to review. Monitor access anomalies, retrieval across boundaries, unexpected sensitive fields, deletion failures, and supplier changes. Give an owner authority to suspend ingestion while investigating.

A privacy review is not finished by a favorable contract. Test the controls periodically and make it possible for people to report a wrong summary or inappropriate disclosure. Keep an incident record that supports assessment under the relevant legal regime. For PIPEDA-covered organizations, the Office of the Privacy Commissioner explains that all breaches require records, while breaches presenting a real risk of significant harm require reporting and notification. GDPR has different breach notification tests and deadlines. Counsel must classify each actual incident, including provincial Canadian obligations where relevant.

Put a short decision before the executive: value, evidence of lawful and limited processing, remaining uncertainty, data-flow owner, monitoring, and stop conditions. Defer a live-data rollout if the supplier cannot explain where personal data goes or how it can be deleted.

example.title: A pilot with a boundary
example.body: Approve 30 days of call summaries for one trained team using an approved transcript field set. Disable provider training, restrict access, sample outputs and logs weekly, and require a verified deletion test. Any expansion to coaching or model improvement needs a separate purpose review. The duration is illustrative.

exercise.title: Write the data-use approval
exercise.body: In one page, specify purpose, classes, users, region, supplier setting, retention, rights process, owner, monitoring, and stop trigger. Then describe one product change that requires a new privacy review.

sources: Office of the Privacy Commissioner: PIPEDA breach reporting
